title: What owners want, and why they buy
source: Field Guide 00a (roles: the owner and GM cards, where roles pull against each other) and the dashboard itself: the demo company (scripts/training-video/cost/seed.py) on a local copy, 20 Nov 2026

scenes.title: What owners want, and why they buy
beats: In episode one, we saw how a construction company works, and where its money leaks.
Now, let's meet the person who decides whether to buy Mesiri: the owner.
And this time, we'll see the software itself.

lines.text: The owner buys. The site uses it.
The owner's questions, and the screens that answer them

scenes.title: Rarely on site, always on the phone
beats: The owner, or managing director, spends the day winning work, meeting clients and banks, and finding cash.
They hear about their sites by phone, and in meetings, from memory.
They won't enter data. They won't learn a complicated system. And they won't read long reports.
So whatever we show them has to fit on one screen, or in one message.

cards.title: Their day
cards.text: Winning work, clients, banks, cash, a few big decisions.

cards.title: How they hear
cards.text: Phone calls and meetings. Answers from memory.

cards.title: Won't do
cards.text: Enter data. Learn a complex system. Read long reports.

cards.title: What works
cards.text: One screen, or one message: profit, cash, risks.

scenes.title: Four questions every owner carries
beats: Every owner carries the same four questions.
One: which projects are making money, and which are losing it?
Two: how much cash will I need next month?
Three: who owes me money, and whom do I owe?
And four: is anything going badly wrong, right now?
Keep these four in mind. The screens in this episode answer them.

scenes.title: Often the one who decides
beats: In bigger companies, the general manager often decides on the purchase.
The general manager we met asked one question, again and again.
Was fifteen thousand rupees of work done, for the fifteen thousand we paid?
What they want is green or red for every project, every day; approvals in one place, with the facts beside them; and what material came, what was used, and what's missing.

scenes.eyebrow: Why they buy, why they quit
scenes.title: One real loss, caught early
beats: Here's what decides whether an owner keeps using software.
They adopt it when it catches one real loss, early. Just one is enough.
They quit when its numbers disagree with their accountant, or with their general manager.
So in a pitch, we never promise everything. We show one leak, caught the same day, with numbers they can trust.

items: It catches one real loss early

right.title: Quits when
items: Its numbers disagree with Tally or the GM

footer.text: Pitch: one leak, caught the same day, with numbers they trust.

scenes.title: The owner wants detail. The site wants to type less.
beats: But there's a catch. The owner wants detail, and the engineer on site wants to type as little as possible.
Most software takes the owner's side, with long forms for the site. So the site stops using it, and the owner's screens go empty.
Mesiri settles it differently: the site speaks, and the owner reads.

middle.text: Long forms → the site stops → the owner's screens go empty

footer.text: Mesiri: the site speaks, the owner reads.

scenes.title: The site speaks, on WhatsApp
beats: On site, the engineer already uses WhatsApp all day. So that's where Mesiri listens.
They send a line, or a voice note, in Malayalam, Manglish or English. Like this: Main block, six masons, four helpers, plinth beam shuttering done.
Mesiri understands it, and replies with a card: the attendance and the work, ready to save.
One tap, and it's recorded. No app to install, and no form to fill.

scenes.title: Every site's day, as it happens
beats: In the office, every message lands here, on the Today page.
All four sites have reported. Thirty-seven workers are on site, and there are three open issues.
Each site shows its workers, its work and its material, with the engineer's own words.
And the worst problems come first: an inspection the slab pour is waiting for, and cement that may run short by Friday.

scenes.title: The owner's morning, on one screen
beats: This is the owner's home page. It answers the four questions on one screen.
Who owes me, and whom do I owe? Clients owe twenty-one lakh rupees. The company owes suppliers thirty-three lakh. And one point seven lakh of wages are due.
Which project is slipping? One of two is over budget: Lake View Apartments.
And what needs me this week? Approve the wages. Check the costs on Lake View. Raise the next bill to the client. Chase the payment that's late.
Problems are pushed to the owner, not hunted for.

scenes.title: Which projects make money, and which lose it
beats: Question one, in detail: is each project making money?
Cost control compares what was spent with the value of the work actually done.
Lake View Apartments is red: its spending is running ahead of its work, and it's heading over budget. Green Villa is green.
And it points to what's still missing: labour and work that haven't been put on the BOQ yet, so the picture is complete.

scenes.title: The owner's board
beats: And then there's Live: the owner's board, updated as the messages arrive from site.
Caught today: one delivery came in above its order's rate. A thousand rupees, caught the same day.
Is anything leaking? A supplier billed two thousand four hundred rupees more than was delivered.
What do I owe, and who owes me? Wages, advances, supplier bills, and work that can be billed to the client right now.
And what will stop work tomorrow? Cement at Main block is below its minimum, and it isn't ordered yet.
Remember leaks one and six from episode one? Here they are, caught on the day, not at month end.

scenes.title: Show what's ready. Check the rest.
beats: One last thing, before any pitch: be honest about what's ready.
Capture on WhatsApp, Today, daily reports, issues, materials, cost control and Live: you've just seen them working.
Other parts, like accounts and the Tally link, are newer. Check what's switched on for a customer before you promise it.
Remember: an owner quits when the numbers disagree. Over-promising is the fastest way to lose one.

scenes.title: The owner buys. The site uses it.
beats: So: the owner buys, and the site uses it. The owner wants answers, not registers. And they stay when Mesiri catches a real loss, early.
In episode three, we'll spend one whole day at Green Villa: from the first WhatsApp message in the morning, to the owner's report at night.
